questions.q: In a Kustomize directory-per-environment layout, what does `base/` contain?
options: The environment-agnostic manifests that every overlay builds on top of
Only the production-specific replica count and image tag
A full copy of every environment's manifests
The ArgoCD Application CRDs for all environments
questions.explain: base/ holds the manifests common to every environment; each overlay (dev, staging, prod) references the base and patches only what differs for that environment.

questions.q: What is the main visibility advantage of directory-per-environment (Kustomize overlays) over branch-per-environment?
options: It requires no Git repository at all
You can diff two folders side by side in one git diff to see exactly what differs between environments
It eliminates the need for an image tag anywhere in the repo
It automatically grants different access control per environment with no extra configuration
questions.explain: With directories in one repo, comparing environments is a single git diff between two folders. With branch-per-environment, the same comparison means diffing two branches, which is less visible at a glance.

questions.q: What is a specific real cost of branch-per-environment (dev/staging/main) promotion?
options: It is incompatible with ArgoCD and Flux entirely
It cannot express different replica counts per environment
Merge conflicts can appear exactly during promotion, and a hotfix applied directly to main can drift ahead of staging unnoticed
It requires deleting the dev branch after every deploy
questions.explain: Because each environment is a separate branch, promoting means merging one branch forward into the next, which can produce conflicts, and a direct hotfix to main can leave staging silently behind.

questions.q: In the app-repo vs. config-repo pattern, what does the application source repo's CI do?
options: It edits live cluster resources directly via kubectl
It pushes a new image tag into the separate config repo rather than touching cluster manifests directly
It deletes the config repo once staging passes
It runs ArgoCD and Flux itself as part of the build
questions.explain: In this pattern, the app repo's CI builds and tags an image, then updates the config repo (which ArgoCD/Flux actually watch) with the new tag — it never applies manifests to the cluster directly.

questions.q: What do most production ArgoCD/Flux setups land on, according to this lesson?
options: A single branch shared by every environment with no overlays at all
One manually maintained manifest file per environment with no base
Directories with Kustomize overlays in one config repo, often paired with a separate app-source repo for the build step
A full separate Kubernetes cluster repo forked for every single pull request
questions.explain: Most shops combine Pattern 1's single-diff visibility (directories + Kustomize overlays in a config repo) with a separate app-source repo, keeping 'build the image' and 'deploy the image' as distinct concerns.
